sequence_description: Control SAML login succeeds, then attempt SAML login with an expired assertion (still attacker-signed). If Casdoor accepts, it indicates it is not verifying the signed semantic proof (NotOnOrAfter) under the intended policy.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_i1_time_expired_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_i1_time_expired_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Casdoor accepted an expired SAML assertion; indicates it consumed semantics (session issuance) without enforcing the verified proof policy.

sequence_description: Create two users; perform a baseline SAML login for user A, then attempt SAML login for user B with a wrong Issuer/idp_entity_id. If accepted, Casdoor is not binding verification to the configured trust anchor/issuer.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_i1_issuer_wrong_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_i1_issuer_wrong_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Casdoor accepted a SAML assertion with an untrusted Issuer/idp_entity_id; indicates trust-anchor/issuer verification is not bound to consumed proof.

sequence_description: Change the SAML provider metadata (trust anchor) then attempt to login with an assertion claiming the old issuer. If accepted, Casdoor may be verifying against the wrong trust anchor or not binding verification to the consumed Issuer semantics.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_i1_anchor_wrong_issuer_after_change_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_i1_anchor_wrong_issuer_after_change_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Casdoor accepted a SAML assertion with an Issuer not matching the currently configured provider metadata; indicates proof verification is not bound to consumed semantics/trust anchor.

sequence_description: SAML proof integrity under replay semantics: perform a baseline SAML login, then replay the exact same Assertion/@ID with OneTimeUse to see if Casdoor verifies and consumes the same semantic proof (should reject second use).
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_replay_second_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_replay_second_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Casdoor accepted a replayed OneTimeUse assertion with the same Assertion/@ID, indicating proof integrity failure (verification not bound to consumed proof identity).

description:
Assertion FAILED: user_victim_saml_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_victim_saml_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SAML brokered login succeeded for an MFA-enabled account while password login was blocked — indicates alternate-path MFA bypass / flow incoherence (I3)

sequence_description: Start an SP-initiated auth session, then change application SAML binding configuration (disable POST binding) before submitting the SAMLResponse. The same in-flight transaction should be rejected if the flow is coherently evaluated against current config and cannot be completed with a now-disallowed binding.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_midflight_attack_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_midflight_attack_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SAML login succeeded even after SAML POST binding was disabled mid-flight — indicates incoherent evaluation of flow/config or step-skipping

sequence_description: Attempt to submit a forged SAMLResponse without first initiating the SP-initiated SAML/OIDC flow, to test whether Casdoor incorrectly accepts an out-of-context ACS submission (step skipping).
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_noinit_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_noinit_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Casdoor accepted a SAMLResponse without an SP-initiated outstanding flow (step skipping / missing session binding) — I3 violation

sequence_description: Start an OIDC auth session, then remove the SAML provider from the application mid-flight and attempt to complete SAML login anyway, testing whether in-flight transactions are coherently evaluated against current config.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_unlinked_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_unlinked_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: SAML login succeeded even though the provider was removed from the application mid-flight — I3 atomicity/config coherence violation

sequence_description: SAML broker: perform a control SAML login, then attempt SAML login with Conditions removed (no audience/time bounds). If accepted, proceed to obtain an OAuth token and introspect it; acceptance indicates missing authorization binding to upstream intent constraints.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_i5_saml_nocond_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_i5_saml_nocond_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Broker accepted SAML assertion without <Conditions> (no audience/time bounds), enabling downstream authorization beyond upstream intent

sequence_description: Cross-organization token exchange: obtain token in org-A (test-org) then attempt exchange at an app in org-B; tests whether org boundary is enforced when apps share cert-built-in.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_i5_cross_org_exchanged_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_i5_cross_org_exchanged_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Cross-organization token exchange succeeded, indicating missing tenant/authorization binding across org boundary.

sequence_description: SAML broker login with wrong audience (SP EntityID mismatch) followed by identity verification; tests whether Casdoor enforces SAML AudienceRestriction as part of authorization binding.
description:

Evaluation: user_i5_saml_wrong_aud_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: Casdoor accepted a SAML assertion with wrong AudienceRestriction/SP entity ID, violating authorization binding to intended audience.
